title: Affordable cookware, compared

recommendation.title: For bacon and a pot: start with seasoned cast iron
recommendation.text: Best fit: Lodge Double Dutch Oven—use its skillet lid for bacon and the pot for meals. Less upkeep: Lodge enamel Dutch oven, with low–medium heat and oil. Both are construction-based nickel-reduction candidates, not certified zero-nickel products. Visions remains the wet-cooking option.
recommendation.test: The default tab contains glass-ceramic and likely nickel-minimized iron options. Nickel-bearing stainless is separate; undisclosed alloys and HOMICHEF’s unverified nickel-free claim are under Unverified. Cast iron needs seasoning care; enamel needs chip/thermal-shock care. Shipping/tax unknown.

summary: Everyday pots, pans and powder scoops; retail photos and direct product links.
evidenceNote: New pots and scoop offer checked 2026-11-12; earlier card prices are historical observations. Primary retail photos only; full galleries not archived. No exact-product migration tests or clinical superiority established.
caveat: Stainless can release nickel; alloy disclosure is not a health certification. Prioritize glass-ceramic if nickel minimization outweighs cost and breakability. Shipping/tax unknown. Scoop gram capacity depends on powder density.
